name: FIN6
summary: FIN6 is a cyber crime group that has stolen payment card data and sold it for profit on underground marketplaces. This group has aggressively targeted and compromised point of sale (PoS) systems in the hospitality and retail sectors.

procedures.text: FIN6 has obtained and used tools such as Mimikatz, Cobalt Strike, and AdFind.
To move laterally on a victim network, FIN6 has used credentials stolen from various systems on which it gathered usernames and password hashes.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a domain user account.
FIN6 has targeted victims with e-mails containing malicious attachments.
FIN6 has used fake job advertisements sent via LinkedIn to spearphish targets.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use known credentials to run commands and spawn processes as a local user account.
FIN6 has used `kill.bat` script to disable security tools.
FIN6 has used WMI to automate the remote execution of PowerShell scripts.
FIN6 has used scheduled tasks to establish persistence for various malware it uses, including downloaders known as HARDTACK and SHIPBREAD and FrameworkPOS.
FIN6 has used PowerShell to gain access to merchant's networks, and a Metasploit PowerShell module to download and execute shellcode and to set up a local listener.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can use Native API including `GetProcAddress` and `ShellExecuteW`.
FIN6 has created Windows services to execute encoded PowerShell commands.
FIN6 has used malicious JavaScript to steal payment card data from e-commerce sites.
FIN6 has used scripting to iterate through a list of compromised PoS systems, copy data to a log file, and remove the original data files.
FIN6 has used malicious documents to lure victims into allowing execution of PowerShell scripts.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use VBA to perform execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Python to perform execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can download a hosted "beacon" payload using BITSAdmin.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can exploit Oracle Java vulnerabilities for execution, including CVE-2011-3544, CVE-2013-2465, CVE-2012-4681, and CVE-2013-2460.
FIN6 has used Registry Run keys to establish persistence for its downloader tools known as HARDTACK and SHIPBREAD.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can install a new service.

Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper has been extended to include Skeleton Key domain controller authentication bypass functionality. The `LSADUMP::ChangeNTLM` and `LSADUMP::SetNTLM` modules can also manipulate the password hash of an account without knowing the clear text value.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can modify Registry values within `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\<Excel Version>\Excel\Security\AccessVBOM\` to enable the execution of additional code.
PsExec: PsExec has the ability to remotely create accounts on target systems.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to use an Excel Workbook to execute additional code by enabling Office to trust macros and execute code without user permission.
Ryuk: Ryuk has used Wake-on-Lan to power on turned off systems for lateral movement.
Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper contains an implementation of an SSP.

FIN6 has used tools to exploit Windows vulnerabilities in order to escalate privileges. The tools targeted CVE-2013-3660, CVE-2011-2005, and CVE-2010-4398, all of which could allow local users to access kernel-level privileges.
FIN6 has used has used Metasploit’s named-pipe impersonation technique to escalate privileges.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can inject a variety of payloads into processes dynamically chosen by the adversary.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to load DLLs via reflective injection.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use process hollowing for execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can steal access tokens from exiting processes.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can make tokens from known credentials.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can spawn processes with alternate PPIDs.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `MISC::AddSid` module can append any SID or user/group account to a user's SID-History. Mimikatz also utilizes SID-History Injection to expand the scope of other components such as generated Kerberos Golden Tickets and DCSync beyond a single domain.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use a number of known techniques to bypass Windows UAC.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `sudo` to run a command.
FIN6 has removed files from victim machines.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent has used Rotate on Right (RoR) and Rotate on Left (RoL) functionality to encrypt strings.
FIN6 has renamed the "psexec" service name to "mstdc" to masquerade as a legitimate Windows service.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can use a decryption algorithm for strings based on Rotate on Right (RoR) and Rotate on Left (RoL) functionality.
FIN6 has used encoded PowerShell commands.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has been installed via `msiexec.exe`.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has used `rundll32` for execution.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent has the ability to add bytes to change the file hash.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike includes a capability to modify the Beacon payload to eliminate known signatures or unpacking methods.
More_eggs: More_eggs's payload has been encrypted with a key that has the hostname and processor family information appended to the end.
Maze: Maze has inserted large blocks of junk code, including some components to decrypt strings and other important information for later in the encryption process.
Ryuk: Ryuk can create.dll files that actually contain a Rich Text File format document.

Ryuk: Ryuk has constructed legitimate appearing installation folder paths by calling `GetWindowsDirectoryW` and then inserting a null byte at the fourth character of the path. For Windows Vista or higher, the path would appear as `C:\Users\Public`.
Maze: Maze has used the “Wow64RevertWow64FsRedirection” function following attempts to delete the shadow volumes, in order to leave the system in the same state as it was prior to redirection.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can timestomp any files or payloads placed on a target machine to help them blend in.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can delete previously created tasks on a compromised host.
More_eggs: More_eggs has used regsvr32.exe to execute the malicious DLL.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent uses the last 64 bytes of the binary to compute a mutex name. If the generated name is invalid, it will default to the generic `mymutex`.
Cobalt Strike: The Cobalt Strike loader can use the `MessageBoxA` API to prompt for user interaction as an anti-sandbox measure.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can sleep for 195 - 205 seconds after payload execution and before deleting its task.

Maze: Maze operators have used VirtualBox and a Windows 7 virtual machine to run the ransomware; the virtual machine's configuration file mapped the shared network drives of the target company, presumably so Maze can encrypt files on the shared drives as well as the local machine.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use spoof arguments in spawned processes that execute beacon commands.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike's `execute-assembly` command can run a.NET executable within the memory of a sacrificial process by loading the CLR.
FIN6 has deployed a utility script named `kill.bat` to disable anti-virus.
FIN6 has used Comodo code-signing certificates.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCShadow` module can be used to make AD updates by temporarily setting a computer to be a DC.
Ryuk: Ryuk can launch `icacls <path> /grant Everyone:F /T /C /Q` to delete every access-based restrictions on files and directories.
FIN6 has used Windows Credential Editor for credential dumping.
FIN6 has used the Stealer One credential stealer to target e-mail and file transfer utilities including FTP.
FIN6 has used the Stealer One credential stealer to target web browsers.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can recover hashed passwords.
FIN6 has used Metasploit’s PsExec NTDSGRAB module to obtain a copy of the victim's Active Directory database.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can collect keyboard events.
FIN6 has extracted password hashes from ntds.dit to crack offline.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from the LSA.

procedures.text: FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can collect mouse events.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO::Extract` module can extract keys by interacting with Windows cryptographic application programming interface (API) functions.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz contains functionality to acquire credentials from the Windows Credential Manager.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create golden tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's kerberos module can create silver tickets.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO` module can create and export various types of authentication certificates.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can enumerate the IP and domain of a target system.

FIN6 used publicly available tools (including Microsoft's built-in SQL querying tool, osql.exe) to map the internal network and conduct reconnaissance against Active Directory, Structured Query Language (SQL) servers, and NetBIOS.
FrameworkPOS: FrameworkPOS can enumerate and exclude selected processes on a compromised host to speed execution of memory scraping.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can collect the victim's operating system and computer name during the initial infection.
FIN6 has used Metasploit’s PsExec NTDSGRAB module to obtain a copy of the victim's Active Directory database.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy enumerates the current user during the initial infection.

FIN6 used publicly available tools (including Microsoft's built-in SQL querying tool, osql.exe) to map the internal network and conduct reconnaissance against Active Directory, Structured Query Language (SQL) servers, and NetBIOS.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent has the ability to enumerate files and directories on a compromised host.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent has used `Accept-Language` to identify hosts in the United Kingdom, United States, France, and Spain.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can produce a sessions report from compromised hosts.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy enumerates the privilege level of the victim during the initial infection.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can identify targets by querying account groups on a domain contoller.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy will attempt to detect anti-virus products during the initial infection.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can enumerate services on compromised hosts.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can query `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Office\<Excel Version>\Excel\Security\AccessVBOM\` to determine if the security setting for restricting default programmatic access is enabled.
More_eggs: More_eggs has used HTTP GET requests to check internet connectivity.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy will attempt to detect if a usable smart card is current inserted into a card reader.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can query shared drives on the local system.
AdFind: AdFind can gather information about organizational units (OUs) and domain trusts from Active Directory.

procedures.text: Cobalt Strike: The Cobalt Strike System Profiler can discover applications through the browser and identify the version of Java the target has.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can identify the country code on a compromised host.
Ryuk: Ryuk has called `GetLogicalDrives` to emumerate all mounted drives, and `GetDriveTypeW` to determine the drive type.
FIN6 used RDP to move laterally in victim networks.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Window admin shares (C$ and ADMIN$) for lateral movement.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can perform pass the hash.
PsExec: PsExec can be used to download or upload a file over a network share.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can deliver Beacon payloads for lateral movement by leveraging remote COM execution.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can SSH to a remote service.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `WinRM` to execute a payload on a remote host.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCSync` and `KERBEROS::PTT` modules implement the three steps required to extract the krbtgt account hash and create/use Kerberos tickets.
FIN6 has collected and exfiltrated payment card data from compromised systems.
FIN6 has encoded data gathered from the victim with a simple substitution cipher and single-byte XOR using the 0xAA key, and Base64 with character permutation.
FIN6 actors have compressed data from remote systems and moved it to another staging system before exfiltration.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can capture screenshots.
FIN6 has used a script to iterate through a list of compromised PoS systems, copy and remove data to a log file, and to bind to events from the submit payment button.
FIN6 has collected schemas and user accounts from systems running SQL Server.
Following data collection, FIN6 has compressed log files into a ZIP archive prior to staging and exfiltration.
FrameworkPOS: FrameworkPOS can identifiy payment card track data on the victim and copy it to a local file in a subdirectory of C:\Windows\.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can collect clipboard data.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can perform browser pivoting and inject into a user's browser to inherit cookies, authenticated HTTP sessions, and client SSL certificates.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has used HTTP for C2.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy can transfer files from C2.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has used SEAL encryption during the initial C2 handshake.
FIN6 used the Plink command-line utility to create SSH tunnels to C2 servers.
FIN6 has used Metasploit Bind and Reverse TCP stagers.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can base64 encode C2 replies.
FIN6 used the Plink command-line utility to create SSH tunnels to C2 servers.
FIN6 has used Pastebin and Google Storage to host content for their operations.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy may obfuscate portions of the initial C2 handshake.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can pad C2 messages with random generated values.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can leverage the HTTP protocol for C2 communication, while hiding the actual data in either an HTTP header, URI parameter, the transaction body, or appending it to the URI. Cobalt Strike
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can conduct peer-to-peer communication over Windows named pipes encapsulated in the SMB protocol. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use a custom command and control protocol that can be encapsulated in DNS. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can be configured to have commands relayed over a peer-to-peer network of infected hosts. This can be used to limit the number of egress points, or provide access to a host without direct internet access.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to accept a value for HTTP Host Header to enable domain fronting.
Maze: Maze has forged POST strings with a random choice from a list of possibilities including "forum", "php", "view", etc. while making connection with the C2, hindering detection efforts.
FlawedAmmyy: FlawedAmmyy has sent data collected from a compromised host to its C2 servers.
FIN6 has sent stolen payment card data to remote servers via HTTP POSTs.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can set its Beacon payload to reach out to the C2 server on an arbitrary and random interval.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike will break large data sets into smaller chunks for exfiltration.
FrameworkPOS: FrameworkPOS can use DNS tunneling for exfiltration of credit card data.
LockerGoga: LockerGoga had blocked network communications by disabling all the network interfaces on the system via netsh.exe.
LockerGoga: LockerGoga has disabled all the network interfaces on the system via netsh.exe to include Wi-Fi.

Maze: Maze has disrupted systems by encrypting files on targeted machines, claiming to decrypt files if a ransom payment is made. Maze has used the ChaCha algorithm, based on Salsa20, and an RSA algorithm to encrypt files.

LockerGoga: While Norsk Hydro attempted to recover from a LockerGoga infection, most of its 160 manufacturing locations switched to manual (non-IT driven) operations. Manual operations can result in a loss of productivity.
Maze: Maze has stopped SQL services to ensure it can encrypt any database.
Maze: Maze has attempted to delete the shadow volumes of infected machines, once before and once after the encryption process.
Maze: Maze has issued a shutdown command on a victim machine that, upon reboot, will run the ransomware within a VM.
LockerGoga: Some of Norsk Hydro's production systems were impacted by a LockerGoga infection. This resulted in a loss of control which forced the company to switch to manual operations.
LockerGoga: Some of Norsk Hydro's production systems were impacted by a LockerGoga infection. This resulted in a loss of view which forced the company to switch to manual operations.
LockerGoga: LockerGoga has been observed changing account passwords and logging off current users.
